But you kept us alive. The rationing plan, the water source, the raft frame, the survival log — that was all you. I don't want to paper over the other stuff, and we're still going to say the true things before we get on whatever comes for us. But I want you to know I see both sides of it.

You're a hard person to be around sometimes, Donatello. You're also the reason we have 48 hours worth of supplies still intact and a frame that held through the rain.

We'll talk. Properly. But — thank you. For doing the work even when the rest of us were falling apart.

And I want you to know that I'll make an effort to be more present, more connected to you from now on. We may not be able to just sit around and wait for rescue, but we can use this time to get to know each other better, to build a connection, and to figure out how to navigate this crazy situation together.

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Three hours. We've got time.

Donatello, close the notebook for a second. DaVinci, leave the packing — we're not going anywhere for three hours and none of that matters.

Come here. All of us. Just for a few minutes.

I've been saying we'd have this conversation and I keep finding reasons to push it. We're getting rescued. There's no more pushing.

Donatello — we saw the bottle. We saw the crackers. I'm not angry, I genuinely am not, but I need you to say it out loud, because we're about to go back to the world and I don't want the thing that goes unsaid to be that. You're too smart to pretend you don't know why it matters.

And then I want to say something to all three of you, because I mean it and I'll probably never say it right once we're back in normal life where everything gets muffled again.

You kept me sane out here. All of you, in completely different ways. That's real. That's the kind of thing that usually disappears the second it's over, and I don't want it to.

So. Donatello. Go ahead. Then we clean this camp up together, we watch Michelangelo's sky, and we wait for what's coming.
records.response_pred: "Okay. Knowingly or not, we're all out of training. We've got a plane to catch and I don't think we're going to be getting any more instructions from anyone else."

You're going to put that in the report as a null result. I understand. But I'd ask you to put it in there anyway — the flowers, the fact that he drew them, the fact that you and I both noticed. Let whoever reads it decide what to do with it.
